reason: Session settled the naming of refs and their placement on the map: @ always reads address first, a ref is a stable record with a unique ref_id named address@ref_id, and files are placed by an agent's explicit link rather than automatic matching. Held tickets code.graph.knowledge#c and code.analyzer.refactoring#1a depend on this, and no skill records it yet.

Linking a file to an element is now a dispatch verb (dispatch_link), and the obvious alternative, map knowledge add-element with refs, silently replaces an element's sources refs. The skill must steer agents to the safe call and away from the destructive one.

An agent editing a CHANGELOG and test file hit the file-access gate; the refusal text says the link must come first. This skill covers linking but not that the gate blocks edits until the link exists, so an agent would otherwise learn it from a refusal.
The ref form changed this session: the id leads and the join closes the name. The old address-first form in this skill is now wrong and would mislead agents naming refs.
The code-link path and the automatic matcher were removed this session; the skill still tells agents to use a removed verb.
Status line goes stale as tickets move; record the state as of this date and keep the rule to read the ticket first.
The episode bypassed the link gate by editing through a script and linked only afterwards; the skill covers the Edit tool but not scripted writes, and its dated status line is stale.
